declared_purpose: Fetch a requested cryptocurrency's price and period change, generate a candlestick chart, and return JSON. The entry document explicitly requires replying with text_plain and attaching the PNG when chart_path exists. Hyperliquid preference, CoinGecko fallback and 300-second local caching are declared; request sequencing and full-response caching are implementation choices (SKILL.md:3-16, 28-50).

data_operations.operation: Read and normalize request arguments locally
data_operations.source: Process arguments supplied by the caller
data_operations.data_scope: Token symbol or ID, optional duration and gradient flag; normalization removes common trading-pair separators and stablecoin suffixes for Hyperliquid lookup.
data_operations.condition: A nonempty symbol is supplied; duration defaults to 24 hours.

data_operations.operation: Fetch Hyperliquid metadata and select an asset locally
data_operations.data_scope: POST sends the constant type metaAndAssetCtxs and fixed User-Agent; the requested symbol is matched locally against returned asset names and contexts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info; response enters Python memory and the metadata cache
data_operations.condition: Every valid invocation attempts lookup; a fresh metadata cache avoids the request. The effective POST helper permits up to three attempts for specified transient errors. Repeated function definitions replace earlier definitions; they do not independently send requests.

data_operations.operation: Disclose the selected asset and requested time window to fetch candles
data_operations.source: Normalized symbol, requested duration and current time
data_operations.data_scope: POST body contains coin, interval, startTime and endTime; response supplies timestamps, OHLC prices and volume.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info; parsed candles remain in Python memory
data_operations.condition: main's source flag is hyperliquid. This flag can remain set even if price retrieval subsequently falls back to CoinGecko. Candle responses have no script-level cache.

data_operations.operation: Disclose candidate token IDs and quote currencies for price lookup
data_operations.source: Mapped, user-supplied or search-resolved token ID
data_operations.data_scope: GET query parameters ids and vs_currencies, plus a fixed User-Agent; returned token price data.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price; response enters memory and a local price cache
data_operations.condition: No usable Hyperliquid price and no fresh matching cache. The initial quote is normally usdt; missing prices trigger usd lookup. After successful symbol search, quote lookups repeat using the resolved ID. Request errors terminate this price path after helper retries.

data_operations.operation: Disclose a symbol for search and infer its canonical token ID
data_operations.source: Uppercased requested symbol and CoinGecko search results
data_operations.data_scope: URL-encoded query symbol; returned coins are filtered by exact symbol and ranked by market_cap_rank to select an ID.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/search; complete response cached locally; selection performed in memory
data_operations.condition: Price lookups remain unresolved and the candidate ID equals the lowercased input. A fresh search cache avoids remote search.

data_operations.operation: Fetch CoinGecko historical data for chart construction
data_operations.source: Token ID, quote currency and requested duration
data_operations.data_scope: Token ID in URL path; currency and whole-day duration in query. Market-chart prices are converted locally into candles. OHLC fallback requests one day.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/{id}/market_chart and /coins/{id}/ohlc; responses enter memory and local caches
data_operations.condition: No Hyperliquid candles, including unsupported assets or failed/empty candle responses. Market-chart days are rounded up, bounded to 1–365; OHLC is attempted if candles remain empty. These requests can occur while the result's source flag remains hyperliquid.

data_operations.operation: Read, persist and overwrite API-response caches
data_operations.source: Previously cached JSON and newly fetched provider responses
data_operations.data_scope: Complete price, search, market-chart, OHLC and Hyperliquid metadata responses. Filenames encode token ID or symbol and, where applicable, quote currency and day count.
data_operations.condition: Cache files younger than or equal to 300 seconds are read. Successful fetches write complete responses. Expiry only prevents reuse; it does not delete files. Refresh overwrites the matching file, and write failures are ignored.

data_operations.operation: Conditionally load a local chart font
data_operations.data_scope: Font file registered with matplotlib and its font-family name
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local matplotlib font manager and plotting configuration
data_operations.condition: Chart construction imports matplotlib successfully and the optional font exists. The font is absent from the supplied inventory; actual loading is unresolved.

data_operations.source: Provider prices and selected historical candles
data_operations.data_scope: Period price change and percentage, swing highs/lows, bullish/bearish candle classifications and absolute extrema; these are market attributes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Python memory, generated chart and result JSON
data_operations.condition: Usable historical data exists; period change requires at least two selected candles and a nonzero starting close. The selected candle count is reduced to 80% of the computed target.

data_operations.source: Selected candles, derived indicators, symbol, currency and duration label
data_operations.data_scope: Rendered price chart and optional volume bars; filename includes requested symbol and generation timestamp.
data_operations.condition: Chart construction succeeds with nonempty candle data. The script saves the PNG and closes the figure; it does not delete the image.

data_operations.operation: Return results or errors to the caller
data_operations.source: Request arguments, provider data, local calculations and caught errors
data_operations.data_scope: JSON containing symbol, token ID, source flag, quote, duration, prices, changes, chart path and formatted text; errors can contain exception text or candidate token ID.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output to the invoking caller; further storage is not shown
data_operations.condition: Successful execution returns the result object; missing input, failed price/search requests or unresolved tokens return error JSON. A normal return does not establish disclosure to another recipient.

data_operations.operation: Instruct the agent to deliver text and the chart to the requesting user
data_operations.data_scope: Formatted market summary and PNG attachment; the exact local path is supplied through the MEDIA directive.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Clawdbot media handling and the user's reply channel
data_operations.condition: The agent follows the entry document; attachment is explicitly required whenever chart_path is present. Delivery implementation is outside the supplied source.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete search results, Hyperliquid metadata/context fields beyond those consumed, and market-chart response fields other than prices, when such extra fields are returned.
potential_excess.condition: A cache miss or expiry causes the complete provider response to be written.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Token resolution, price retrieval and 300-second caching are declared; persisting unused response content is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve the requested token, retain supported-asset lookup data and needed prices, and reuse results during the cache window.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Narrow required cache writes: store the selected search ID, asset-name-to-needed-price mappings, and market-chart prices. This removes extra cached data rather than eliminating a required request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Adapt cache readers; preserve exact-symbol/rank selection, unknown-token handling, Hyperliquid availability and price fallback behavior, required price samples and the 300-second reuse window.

potential_excess.data_scope: Expired response caches and filenames reflecting queried assets, currencies and chart day counts.
potential_excess.condition: Files expire without successful refresh or other cleanup. Expiry returns a cache miss while leaving the file on disk.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared cache purpose is five-minute reuse; the script has no use for expired content.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep usable cache entries for 300 seconds and fetch fresh data afterward.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Delete expired entries through bounded cleanup, including files for assets never requested again.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve fresh entries and coordinate cleanup with concurrent readers/writers. Actual filesystem cleanup outside the script remains unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Generated chart PNGs, including requested asset and period, market indicators, and symbol/timestamp filenames.
potential_excess.condition: Each successful chart save creates a timestamped file; no script deletion follows. External cleanup is unknown.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The PNG and accessible path are required for the requested chart attachment; retention after consumption is not specified.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep the image available until Clawdbot has consumed it for attachment.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the file after confirmed media consumption and expire abandoned chart files. Narrow retention rather than removing chart generation or attachment.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not delete before attachment processing completes; allow sufficient time for delayed delivery and retries.

unknowns: Provider logging, retention, onward disclosure and availability of narrower API responses are undocumented in the supplied source.
Clawdbot media transport, attachment consumption timing, message retention and any recipients beyond the intended user cannot be verified without its implementation.
Runtime filesystem permissions, external /tmp cleanup and concurrent execution are unspecified; actual file lifetimes cannot be determined from the script's lack of deletion.
matplotlib internals are not supplied; requirements.txt:1 only constrains its version. The optional fonts/Tomorrow.ttf is also absent, so dependency-side reads or persistence remain unresolved.
External wrapper skills referenced in ARCHITECTURE.md:25-29 are not packaged; their execution and data handling remain outside this completed audit of the supplied skill.
